Omid Dolatkia <support@avicennaresearch.com>:
Dear Manoj,This is Omid from the tech team. I hope you are doing well. I apologize for the delay in my review, as I had a few high-priority tasks to attend to. I also apologize for the previous email that was sent to you by mistake.Thank you for your efforts in providing the algorithm for analyzing app usage. After reviewing your code, I noticed some cases for the function split_time_across_hours where it may not handle the data correctly, particularly with the CSV file you shared. One example is the usage of the Chrome app, as shown below: study_id user_id date device_id timestamp record_time app_name start_time end_time fg_time_ms last_used 3948 102674 2024-09 e4bc9a9e7344ea58 fa153eff-7047-11ef-a218-db30b16a298d 2024-09-11T14:10:37.631000+0000 com.android.chrome 2024-09-04T23:49:51.305000+0000 2024-09-05T23:49:51.304000+0000 65139 2024-09-05T18:44:41.793000+0000 In this case, the function is unable to correctly split the fg_time_ms for the given start_time and end_time. For example, in the above record, the start_time is 2024-09-04T23:49:51.305000+0000 and the end_time is 2024-09-05T23:49:51.304000+0000, which spans 24 hours. However, the fg_time_ms is only 65,139 ms (approximately 65 seconds), indicating that most of this 24-hour period is idle time. The current implementation assumes continuous usage across the entire duration, leading to inaccurate splits. No worries, though, as after a few data collection cycles, the end_time values should become more continuous, which you can verify in records located in the middle of the CSV.To improve the accuracy of the analysis, I suggest incorporating the last_used field into your calculations. In the example above, the end_time is after the last_used time, which may indicate irrelevant periods of idle time that should not be considered as active usage.Here are my suggestions for improving the data processing and analysis:Preprocessing and Data Cleaning: Remove invalid or incomplete records. Filter out erroneous fg_time_ms values. Handle duplicate entries to avoid skewing results. Adjust last_used and record_time fields to maintain consistency. ```df.dropna( inplace=True, subset=["start_time", "end_time"], ) df = df[df["fg_time_ms"] >= 0] df = df[df.start_time <= df.end_time] df.drop_duplicates( subset=[ "study_id", "user_id", "device_id", "app_name", "start_time", "end_time", "fg_time_ms", "last_used", ], inplace=True, keep="last", ) df["last_used"][(df.end_time == df.start_time)] = df.start_time df["record_time"][(df.end_time > df.record_time)] = df.end_time df.reset_index(drop=True, inplace=True)```Post-processing Adjustments: Remove duplicate entries for app usage sessions. Ensure start_time, end_time, and fg_time_ms fields are consistent and valid. Handle overlapping sessions and correct fg_time_ms values accordingly. Ensure that fg_time_ms accurately reflects the actual foreground usage for each session. Adjust the end_time field based on the last_used timestamp to avoid incorrect idle time inclusion. ```df_list = [] grouped_df = df.groupby( ["study_id", "user_id", "device_id", "app_name", "start_time"], sort=False, as_index=False, ) for _, sub_df in grouped_df: if len(sub_df) > 1: sub_df.sort_values(by=["fg_time_ms", "end_time"], inplace=True) sub_df.drop_duplicates(subset="fg_time_ms", inplace=True) sub_df["start_time"].iloc[1:] = sub_df["end_time"].shift().iloc[1:] sub_df["fg_time_ms"] = sub_df["fg_time_ms"] - sub_df[ "fg_time_ms" ].shift(fill_value=0) sub_df.reset_index(inplace=True, drop=True) sub_df["end_time"][ (sub_df.last_used > sub_df.start_time) & (sub_df.last_used <= sub_df.end_time) ] = sub_df[ (sub_df.last_used > sub_df.start_time) & (sub_df.last_used <= sub_df.end_time) ][ "last_used" ] df_list.append(sub_df) result_df = pd.concat(df_list) result_df = result_df[result_df.fg_time_ms > 0] result_df.reset_index(inplace=True, drop=True) return result_df```Once the data has been cleaned and adjusted, you can apply your logic to the refined dataset. By grouping the data by day and calculating hourly usage based on the corrected fg_time_ms values, you'll achieve more accurate results.Regarding your request for preprocessed data for comparison, I regret to inform you that we are not currently processing app usage data at an hourly or any other granularity.Please feel free to reach out in case of any further questions, Thank you.Best regards,Omid Note: If you feel like your issue is not properly being addressed and want to escalate it, please click here: https://avicennaresearch.com/app/public/zammad/escalate/25943/notfilledyet --Avicenna Research (formerly Ethica Data)4109 - 295 Adelaide St W, Toronto, ON M5V 0L4, Canada Email: support@avicennaresearch.com - Web: https://avicennaresearch.com-- On Thursday, October 17, 2024 at 7:06:15 PM,
